title: Weight-Space Programming on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B: Nine Independent Agent Edits, Random-Direction Controls, and a Missing Attention Mask
tasks_benchmarks: synthetic stress sets (long trailing silence, speech in silence, bilingual)

headline_result.text: All nine Claude Opus edit arms reduced the language-None failure on 70 target clips with 0 newly broken clips and beat their five random-direction controls in 26 of 27 comparisons, but simply restoring a missing encoder attention mask without any weight change fixed as many clips (36) as the best edit.
headline_result.quote: Restoring the mask with no weight change (baseline_windowed, a separate analysis, not part of the WSP protocol) ﬁxes 31 of 40 stress and 5 of 30 hard-TS target clips, matching the best edit and beating the other eight.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 9 agent arms (3 per budget), 5 random controls each

key_claims.claim: All nine edits reduced the target pathology with no newly broken clips and McNemar p < 0.01 on 70 clips.
key_claims.quote: All nine edits reduce it, with 0 newly broken clips and McNemar p < 0.01 on the combined 70 target clips for every arm.

key_claims.claim: Real edits beat each of five norm-matched random-direction controls in 26 of 27 comparisons.
key_claims.quote: The real edit ﬁxes more target clips than each of its ﬁve random controls in 26 of 27 (arm × target set) comparisons.

key_claims.claim: Four arms paid a small but significant clean-WER regression.
key_claims.quote: The price is a small clean-WER regression for four arms (+0.24 to +0.40 pp macro WER, 95% CI excluding 0)

key_claims.claim: Six of nine arms independently edited the same two decoder attention heads.
key_claims.quote: Six of nine arms independently localized the same two decoder attention heads (L20H13 and L21H2).

key_claims.claim: The pathology is mostly an artifact of a missing encoder window mask in the inference backend; edits compensate for it in weight space.
key_claims.quote: We therefore read the pathology as largely an artifact of this inference backend; the edits compensate in weight space for a missing mask.

key_claims.claim: The second, distributed target (bilingual code-switching) was not fixed by any arm.
key_claims.quote: Target B (bilingual code-switching) was not ﬁxed.

limitations_stated.text: Single 0.6B model and one successfully targeted failure; nothing shows WSP works for ASR in general.
limitations_stated.quote: Nothing here shows that weight-space programming works for ASR in general; Target B argues the opposite for distributed errors.

limitations_stated.text: All agents are Claude Opus instances with a shared brief, so convergence is not statistical independence.
limitations_stated.quote: The arms share a model family, a brief that names mechanism families, and the same practice data, so convergence on the same heads is not evidence of statistical independence.

limitations_stated.text: Edits patch a symptom of the inference stack rather than a model defect.
limitations_stated.quote: Edits therefore patch a symptom of the inference stack rather than a model defect; we have not run FA2 (no CUDA).

notes_for_review: The most carefully controlled WSP replication in this set: nine agent arms, norm- and footprint-matched random-direction controls, a single-use held-out test set and paired statistics. Its key finding cuts against the headline: the repaired pathology was caused by a missing attention mask in the qwen-asr sdpa/MPS backend, and restoring the mask (an inference-only fix) did as well as the best weight edit. Weight edits did not fix a distributed failure (code-switching), echoing MIT's Gemma 3 270M null. No gradient fine-tuning comparison; not peer reviewed.
